specs.scene: Overhead flat-lay of a solo operator's workspace, two hands entering from the bottom edge, one holding a pen resting on a printed client intake form, the other adjusting a small webcam; surrounding objects crowd to every edge and overlap one another: an open laptop with a blank screen, a spiral notebook with handwritten workflow sketches, a stack of printed invoices, a wireless card reader, a desk calculator, a coiled cable, a coffee mug with a faint ring stain, a stapler, a small stack of blank sticky notes, and a phone lying face-down with a blank back panel; bare patches of desk surface show between the clustered objects.
specs.source_quote: The runtime is n8n, Make, or Zapier... a hundred bucks a month

recognisable.why: Generic office and invoicing objects read as any freelance desk, not distinctly an AI-implementation business.

legibility.why: The flat-lay by design contains far more than three separately-resolved elements, failing the single-focal-mass test.

curiosity.why: The overlay states a cost figure, not an unresolved judgement the viewer must ponder.

subject.why: No single anchor object or person; attention is diffused across a dozen small items.

credible.why: The $100/month figure is quoted directly from the script in its smallest honest unit.

stakes.why: A $100 monthly cost implies a near-zero-risk entry point that matters directly to the viewer's wallet.

reexpress.why: Clarifies the title's vague '$100' into a precise recurring unit rather than repeating it verbatim.

specs.scene: Documentary photograph of a restaurant host stand near the entrance, the stand's surface holding a closed paper reservation book, a wall-mounted tablet with a blank screen, and a corded phone; a soft-focus dining room glows warmly behind it; no people are in frame; the editorial verdict runs in condensed capital letters across the top third of the image.
specs.source_quote: Your two thousand dollar install becomes a relationship, not a transaction

recognisable.why: A restaurant host stand is an instantly familiar everyday scene requiring no explanation.

legibility.why: One clean focal object, the host stand, with nothing competing for separate resolution.

curiosity.why: The caption asserts a verdict about what the sale 'becomes' that cannot be confirmed by looking, the exact top-quartile pattern in this register.

subject.why: The host stand serves as one clear, distinctive object anchor.

credible.why: No figure is carried, which scores full per the rubric's absence rule.

stakes.why: Implies an ongoing recurring relationship rather than a one-off job, which matters to anyone pricing their own work.

reexpress.why: Surfaces a consequence (relationship, not transaction) the title never states, without repeating its numbers or wording.

specs.scene: A single printed invoice lies flat on a plain wooden desk, one corner curling slightly, a pen resting beside it; the surrounding desk surface is empty and evenly lit by soft window light; no hands or other objects are present; the invoice fills most of the frame.
specs.source_quote: a two thousand dollar project a single operator can sell in a month

recognisable.why: An invoice is a generic office document without a household-level identity, though at least it is a real physical artefact.

legibility.why: Only one object occupies the frame, satisfying the single-focal-mass test cleanly.

curiosity.why: The overlay states a plain figure rather than implying an unresolved verdict.

subject.why: The invoice functions as one clear, distinctive object anchor tied directly to the trade.

credible.why: The $2,000 figure is quoted exactly as the script states it, in its smallest honest per-sale unit.

stakes.why: A concrete achievable sale amount speaks to what the viewer could actually earn, though it is a modest single data point.

reexpress.why: Grounds the title's abstract $5.9 billion in the smallest real transaction size, the clearest form of splitting the work with the title.

specs.scene: A freelance operator kneels beside a restaurant host stand, hands connecting a small tablet computer to a countertop power outlet, the tablet's screen blank; the host stand's notepad sits closed beside them; the dining room behind is softly out of focus; the composition is cropped close with the left half of the frame left clear and blank.
specs.source_quote: The gap was never the software. It was the person

recognisable.why: A restaurant setting with a person doing visible install work is broadly familiar, though slightly less iconic alone than the host stand shot.

legibility.why: Two separately resolved elements, the person and the tablet, place this at the half-credit tier.

curiosity.why: The overlay implies the real answer lies elsewhere without stating it, prompting the viewer to want the explanation.

subject.why: One person mid-action provides a clear human anchor.

credible.why: No figure is carried, which scores full under the rubric's absence rule.

stakes.why: Suggests the viewer's own effort, not tools, is what determines outcome, which is personally relevant but not sharply threat- or gain-coded.

reexpress.why: Delivers a distinct claim about the mechanism absent from the title's wording, avoiding restatement.
